summary: Couch Investor makes his full bull case for Meta (BUY), which he owns and calls extremely undervalued despite a ~26% YTD drawdown. He first addresses the ongoing trial (6-8 weeks, with Zuckerberg and Mosseri expected to testify): internal documents allegedly showing teen harm, while Meta counters that prosecutors cherry-picked emails and that 40% of teens actually felt better using Instagram. On penalties, he dismisses the $1.4T worst case, sketching a Big Tobacco-style $15-200B fine spread over decades as manageable; the real risk would be forced changes to the algorithm or infinite scroll, which he does not expect. He plays a Ben Thompson clip arguing AI's biggest monetization gains are accruing to Google and Meta, whose ad marketplaces act as a global-scale verification machine for AI-generated creative. His DCF — available free — implies ~53% upside even with reduced base-case assumptions (26.5% revenue growth this year tapering down), while the bear case sits only ~2.6% below the current price. He compares the setup to 2022's hated-then-5x rebound, notes improving models (Muse Spark 1.2 near frontier, 'watermelon' coming) and the possibility of Meta selling compute to hyperscalers as a sentiment trigger. He keeps buying shares under $600 and sold a December $500 put he considers 'free money.'
title: I Can't Stay Quiet About Meta Stock Anymore
